cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Who Cares More?
cards.instruction: Turn every favor, memory, sacrifice, and affectionate gesture into evidence that you care more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I kept twelve tickets from our trips. How many did you keep?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: None. I made you that album instead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. And I kept it. Your care is safe because of mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Open it. I put all my tickets inside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm preserving both our collections. Let me get it a waterproof cover.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 compares kept tickets and A3 claims protective superiority, but A5 let me get a cover is ordinary competitive care rather than sustained approval control beyond prefixes.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 gifted album prompts A3 preserving B care; B4 tickets inside prompts A5 protecting both collections. B2 none can mean none retained separately after gifting, but wording is compressed.

relationship.evidence: B2 names an actual gift and B4 reveals its contents, giving A real evidence of B care to appropriate.

heightening.evidence: B4 tickets in the album causes A5 a larger preservation claim and practical protective cover.

specificity.evidence: A1 shared trips and B2 album establish history; B2 none versus B4 all is best clarified as no separate collection, not automatically treated as a contradiction.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 your care safe because mine is specific; A5 cover is earned but the stock rank prefix remains bulky.
